overview: The two nucleic acids that store and express genetic information, distinguished by sugar, bases, strandedness, and stability.
genZNote: DNA keeps the receipts. RNA gets things moving.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Deoxyribonucleic acid — the long-term, double-stranded molecule that stores genetic information.
aspects.valueB: Ribonucleic acid — a typically single-stranded molecule that carries out and regulates gene expression.

aspects.label: Sugar Backbone
aspects.valueA: Deoxyribose (lacks a 2'-OH group), which makes the backbone more chemically stable.
aspects.valueB: Ribose (has a 2'-OH group), which makes RNA more reactive and prone to hydrolysis.

aspects.label: Strandedness / Structure
aspects.valueA: Almost always double-stranded, forming the classic antiparallel double helix.
aspects.valueB: Usually single-stranded, but folds back on itself into complex secondary structures (e.g. tRNA cloverleaf, ribozymes).

aspects.label: Primary Function
aspects.valueA: Long-term storage of genetic information across generations of cells.
aspects.valueB: Executes that information — mRNA carries the message, tRNA delivers amino acids, rRNA builds proteins, and various small RNAs regulate expression.

aspects.label: Cellular Location
aspects.valueA: Predominantly nuclear (plus small amounts in mitochondria/chloroplasts).
aspects.valueB: Made in the nucleus but functions throughout the cell, especially the cytoplasm and ribosomes.

aspects.label: Stability
aspects.valueA: Chemically stable; built for accurate long-term storage and repair.
aspects.valueB: Less stable, often turned over rapidly, which allows gene expression to be dynamically regulated.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Deoxyribose sugar, thymine, double-stranded, information archive.
aspects.valueB: Ribose sugar, uracil, usually single-stranded, functional/working molecule.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Sugar (deoxyribose vs ribose) and base (thymine vs uracil) are the two fastest ways to tell them apart on an exam.
overlay.commonMisconception: RNA is not just a 'temporary DNA' — it has catalytic and regulatory roles DNA cannot perform (e.g. ribozymes, miRNA).
